changes: Playback URL resolution gets priority in the shared 5 requests/second budget, with bounded fairness for other requests.
A confirmed submission receipt and SHA-256 of the input order allow subsequent clicks in the same playlist to select an existing SQL occurrence.
Queue edits, Core reconnects, library revisions, changed input metadata, shuffle/heart mode and nonzero start positions prevent inappropriate queue reuse.
NetEase task progress notifications no longer invalidate catalog and genre indexes; actual catalog changes still do.
Privacy-safe preparation timing separates queue preparation, source resolution and native startup.

realServiceExperiment.profile: isolated QA profile with 13893 catalog tracks
realServiceExperiment.definition: Elapsed time until the real Core command / renderer queue adapter completes; not microphone-measured audible latency.
realServiceExperiment.method: Sequential baseline and optimized runs against the real NetEase service and native engine, using separate audio cache roots. Network and system load were not controlled.
findings: Repeated selections reach source resolution 2-3 ms after Core preparation starts, without rebuilding the complete queue.
The 2956 ms baseline next-track sample spent 2702 ms inside native playback startup.
The 1884 ms optimized repeat-click sample still spent 1144 ms in native startup, so the work does not eliminate all network-source delays.
No improvement is claimed for first uncached clicks from this experiment.
Initial baseline timing omitted the begin marker; only within-phase timing differences are usable for that baseline. Optimized begin timestamps were corrected and regression tested.
